summary: The note describes farm-to-table cook-offs, competitions that pair local farmers with chefs to celebrate locally sourced ingredients and sustainable agriculture. It profiles events in Vermont, California and Oregon in fall 2023, with quotes from farmers, chefs and a blogger. It highlights the community, economic and educational benefits of these events and expects the trend to keep growing.
one_line: Farm-to-table cook-offs in Vermont, California and Oregon in 2023 pair farmers with chefs, boosting local economies, education and sustainable food awareness.
key_facts: The farm-to-table concept uses ingredients from local farms to reduce food's carbon footprint, ensure freshness, and support local economies.
On September 3, 2023, Vermont hosted the "Green Mountain Harvest Cook-off," bringing together farmers and chefs.
On October 15, 2023, California's annual "Sunshine Culinary Clash" featured fresh, organic, locally harvested ingredients.
On September 21, 2023, the "Farm Fresh Culinary Challenge" in Oregon introduced a 'marketplace' concept where spectators wandered through stalls of produce handpicked by the chefs.
Mike and Sarah Bennett, a husband-and-wife farming team from the outskirts of Burlington, Vermont, advocate organic farming and supply several artisanal restaurants with heirloom vegetables.
After the "Green Mountain Harvest Cook-off," the Bennetts saw a substantial uptick in interest from local dining establishments wanting their organic produce on menus.
Sarah Bennett described the effect as "a ripple effect": one event leads to another restaurant partner, supporting the farm and the local economy.
Chef Marina Garcia sourced ingredients for the "Sunshine Culinary Clash" from local cooperative markets and built relationships with growers.
Marina Garcia's dish was roasted root vegetables with a sun-kissed citrus glaze, which was the talk of the event.
Elena Martinez, a food blogger and advocate for locally-sourced cuisine, said seeing, touching and tasting raw ingredients adds a new layer of appreciation.
James Robinson, a chef-instructor, led workshops at the "Farm Fresh Culinary Challenge" and said "We're not just here to cook; we're here to inform."
Workshops and cooking demonstrations let farmers explain techniques and teach attendees about sourcing locally and seasonally.
The note says these events are increasingly appearing in both rural and urban locales and calls them "symposiums of sustainability."
